Short answer: AI can speed up some language and information tasks. It can also be wrong, expose data, or create confident nonsense. Start with a low-risk task and a human check.

What this means for your business

The useful question is not whether the business should use AI. It is which task, what information enters, what error would cost, who checks the result, and whether the workflow still works without it.

What to watch

  • Customer, employee, health, financial, legal, or credential data pasted into an unapproved tool.
  • An answer published without checking the source.
  • Automation sending a promise or decision to a customer.
  • A paid AI feature added before a real task is named.

Do this next

  1. Choose one reversible, non-sensitive task.
  2. Define the correct output and who reviews it.
  3. Test with fake or public information.
  4. Keep, change, or stop based on measured time and error, not hype.

When Little Fight fits

We can map a safe useful workflow and connect it where appropriate. We do not hand important business decisions to a model and call that innovation.
